title: CEO behind 'GTA 6' says AI is helpful for office admin
excerpt: While "GTA 6" avoided AI to create its immersive virtual world, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said it helps with mundane back-office tasks like charts.
content_html:
'GTA 6' was made by humans, but its publisher is all for using AI on admin

By Pete Syme

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-20T14:06:33.504Z

"Grand Theft Auto 6" may have been painstakingly crafted by humans, but the publisher behind it has been embracing AI in its back office.

Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of Take-Two Interactive — which owns the GTA developer Rockstar Games — was asked about AI's role in the firm's finance and legal operations on Thursday's TBPN broadcast.

"People are using this technology to make their work less mundane, more interesting, more value-added, and to be more productive," he said.

"We too, like other corporations, aren't seeing an opportunity to vastly reduce our back-office head count or anything of the sort, and we are spending money on tokens  — which is something to think about," he added. Tokens are bite-sized pieces of data that AI reads and writes.

JPMorgan, Meta, and KPMG are among the companies that have encouraged workers to use AI, including by setting up internal dashboards to track adoption or usage.

Zelnick said that using AI has made it more efficient to complete some banal tasks.

"For example, it's quicker to make a pie chart than it used to be," he said. "Pie charts don't create any value whatsoever. They're nice to look at, but they just don't create value, so if we could have our people spend a lot less time on pie charts, I'd be thrilled."'

'Hand-built'

"GTA 6" launched on Thursday to rave reviews. Metacritic, a review aggregator, ranks it as the best video game ever with a score of 99 based on 151 reviews.

Zelnick has previously emphasized that no generative AI was used to create "GTA 6." While it took 13 years, that care and precision are what make the game successful.

Critics have lauded the immersion. Beyond everyday tasks like fixing a roof or improving the main characters' romantic relationship, the virtual world is replete with detail. Developers created satirical radio stations, a social media app packed with puerile memes, and 30,000 unique NPCs.

"Hand-touched, hand-built, every single part of it is thought about and worked through," Aaron Garbut, "GTA"'s co-studio head, told The New York Times Magazine. "I think you can feel that."

Outside the creative aspects, though, Zelnick believes AI can make parts of the work easier.

"I understand that competitive dynamics might shift, entry barriers might be reduced, but making hits, marketing hits, financing hits, employing creative talent — all that's going to remain very, very difficult," he told TBPN.

"If technology makes parts of it easier, why wouldn't we avail ourselves of that technology?"
